availability.note: CarsGuide new-car listing '2026 Volvo XC60 Plus T8 Phev Dark', 'New: Available to order', $92,990. volvocars.com/au configurator refused by the proxy (403), so availability rests on third parties: CarsGuide 2027 XC60 price page lists this grade at MSRP among 4 current grades; CarExpert 2027 range page's configurator still shows the MY26 T8 Plus Dark/Ultra Dark with drive-away prices; Chasing Cars (22 Sep 2026) calls the T8 Volvo's current PHEV with the long-range car due Q2 2027

listPrice.note: 'prices starting at $92,990' before on-road costs (CarExpert variant page; CarExpert review 9 Jan 2026 and MY26 launch news say 'before on-road costs' in words); CarsGuide 2027 MSRP $92,990; CarExpert Sydney drive-away $99,757 consistent. Chasing Cars (22 Sep 2026) gives 'from $92,683 before on-roads' — unexplained $307 difference, not adopted

batteryKwh.note: 'Useable battery kilowatt hour: 14.9 kWh'; 'Maximum battery kilowatt hour: 18.8 kWh' (gross) on the same page. Auto Express (22 Sep 2026) also gives 18.8 kWh with 14.9 kWh usable. Held value was 14.7

rangeKm.note: Volvo claim 'up to 81 km' WLTP for the 18.8 kWh T8 (cars.co.za, Feb 2026); CarExpert AU spec pages for both grades give 81 km. Rejected: carsales 89 km '(ADR)' and EV Central/CarExpert-news 89 km 'WLTP' — higher than the manufacturer's WLTP best case, so per the direction test not the comparable quantity. Held 79 km (UK 49.1 mi) not re-openable: volvocars.com refused by proxy (403)

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: batteryKwh / rangeKm x 100 = 14.9 / 81 x 100 = 18.4. Published 26.2 kWh/100km 'combined' (CarExpert, EV Central labels it NEDC) not used: 42% off battery/range, a different quantity

combinedRangeKm.note: 81 km WLTP electric + 71 L tank (CarExpert spec page) / 8.4 L/100km x 100 = 81 + 845.2 = 926

fuelConsumptionL100km.note: No published charge-sustaining figure found (volvocars.com blocked). Held 8.4 kept: EV Central (AU, Oct 2025) 'over 8L/100km once the battery was depleted'; Auto Express T6 group test with a depleted battery 32.6 mpg = 8.7 L/100km, and 'near to 30mpg' (9.4) without plugging in. Sits above siblings bmw-x3-phev 7.6, audi-q5-phev 7.8, mercedes-glc-phev 7.8 and the heavier volvo-xc90-phev 7.7 (XC90 ordering looks backwards by mass; flagged in report)

isFuelEfficientForLct.note: combined-cycle label 'Combined: 1.6 L/100km', at or below 3.5

isGreenForVicDuty.note: SRO green car = passenger car with combined CO2 of 120 g/km or less; CarExpert spec page 'CO2 level - g/km combined: 36 g/km'

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: 'Rear seat up; to lower window: 468 L' (SAE), i.e. to the belt line, matching the cargo-cover convention; Chasing Cars also 468 L

towKg.note: 2,250 kg braked / 750 kg unbraked; EV Central also 2,250 kg. Manufacturer tech sheet unreachable (volvocars.com 403)
